content.question: Which article grants the High Courts the power to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights?
content.note:
Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.
This makes the writ jurisdiction of High Courts wider than that of the Supreme Court (which can only issue writs for Fundamental Rights).

content.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act provided the right to form cooperative societies?
content.note:
The 97th Amendment Act, 2011 gave constitutional status and protection to Cooperative Societies.
It made the right to form cooperatives a Fundamental Right (Article 19), added a new DPSP (Article 43B), and inserted Part IXB.
Note: It aims to empower rural India economically.

content.question: Which article relates to the right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14?
content.note:
Article 21A declares that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of 6 to 14 years.
It was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002. Status: This is considered a fundamental human right essential for the development of the child.

content.question: Indian citizenship is granted by which ministry?
content.note:
Indian Citizenship is governed and granted by the Ministry of Home Affairs.
The Citizenship Act, 1955 provides the legal framework for the acquisition and termination of citizenship.
Note: Articles 5 to 11 in Part II of the Constitution deal with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.

content.question: Under which article can the decisions of the Central Administrative Tribunal be challenged in the Supreme Court?
content.note:
Under Article 323A, Administrative Tribunals are established to resolve disputes regarding the recruitment and service conditions of public servants.
Following the L. Chandra Kumar case, decisions of these tribunals can be challenged in the High Courts (and subsequently the Supreme Court).
Note: This article was added by the 42nd Amendment.

content.question: Under which article are provisions made for reservation for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha?
content.note:
Article 330 provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha.
The reservation is based on the proportion of their population in the state.
Note: There is no reservation for these groups in the Rajya Sabha.

content.question: The pension of a High Court judge is charged upon which fund?
content.note:
The pension of a High Court judge is charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
However, their salaries are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State. Reason: This ensures that a judge's retirement benefits are not dependent on a specific state they served in.

content.question: The period between the end of one session and the beginning of the next is called?
content.note:
The period between the Prorogation of a House and its re-assembly in a new session is called a Recess.
During this period, the House does not meet.
Note: This is different from an 'Adjournment', which only terminates a sitting, not the entire session.

content.question: Who can make laws on residual subjects not mentioned in the lists?
content.answer: Parliament or State Legislature, as decided by the Supreme Court.
content.note:
In India, Parliament has the exclusive power to legislate on residuary subjects.
If a dispute arises about which list a subject belongs to, the Supreme Court has the power to interpret the Constitution and decide.
Note: This strengthens the Unitary bias of the Indian federal system.

content.question: The Indian Constitution is described as what type of system?
content.note:
The Indian Constitution is often described as 'Quasi-Federal'.
It has a Federal structure (division of powers) but a Unitary spirit (strong Central government). Expert View: K.C. Wheare famously described India as a 'Quasi-federal' state due to its unique balance.

content.question: Article 370 related to Jammu and Kashmir was abrogated in which year?
content.note:
Article 370, which gave special status to Jammu and Kashmir, was effectively abrogated in 2019.
The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 bifurcated the state into two Union Territories: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.
Note: This removed the separate constitution and flag of J&K.

content.question: According to Article 112, what must be presented before Parliament every financial year?
content.note:
Under Article 112, the President causes to be laid before Parliament an 'Annual Financial Statement'.
This is popularly known as the Union Budget.
Note: It is a statement of the estimated receipts and expenditure of the Government of India for that financial year.

content.question: The tenure of the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission is?
content.answer: Six years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier.
content.note:
The Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission (SPSC) hold office for a term of 6 years or until age 62, whichever is earlier.
They are appointed by the Governor. Important Note: Although appointed by the Governor, they can only be removed by the President.

content.question: In which year did the Supreme Court rule in the Kesavananda Bharati case that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution?
content.note:
In the Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973), the Supreme Court ruled that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
It also introduced the 'Basic Structure Doctrine'. Reversal: This judgment overruled the earlier Berubari Union case (1960), which had held that the Preamble was not a part of the Constitution.

content.question: What is the function of the Pro Tem Speaker?
content.answer: To administer the oath to the members and discharge duties until the permanent Speaker is elected.
content.note:
A Pro Tem Speaker is appointed by the President to administer the oath to newly elected members of the Lok Sabha.
They also enable the House to elect the permanent Speaker. Tradition: Usually, the senior-most member of the House is chosen as the Pro Tem Speaker.

content.question: By which Constitutional Amendment were the titles of former rulers of princely states abolished?
content.note:
The 26th Amendment Act, 1971 abolished the titles and Privy Purses (payments) of the former rulers of princely states.
It aimed to eliminate the remnants of the colonial and feudal past to ensure social equality. Context: This was a major step under the leadership of Indira Gandhi.

content.question: Under which Amendment was reservation for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) introduced?
content.note:
The 103rd Amendment Act, 2019 introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in jobs and admissions.
It amended Articles 15 and 16.
Note: This reservation is for those not covered under the existing reservations for SC, ST, and OBC.

content.question: Which Article is related to the protection of the environment and safeguarding of forests?
content.note:
Article 48A (added by the 42nd Amendment) mandates that the State shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment.
It specifically mentions safeguarding forests and wildlife. Related info: There is a corresponding Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(g) for citizens.

content.question: How many levels of government are mentioned in the Constitution of India?
content.note:
The Constitution provides for a three-tier system of government.
1. The Union (Central), 2. The States, and 3. Local Bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities).
Note: The third tier was given constitutional status through the 73rd and 74th Amendments.

content.question: The first Education Minister of independent India was?
content.note:
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was the first Education Minister of independent India.
He was a key leader in the independence movement and a staunch proponent of a secular education system.
Note: His birthday, November 11, is celebrated as National Education Day.

content.question: Which Article is related to equal justice and free legal aid?
content.note:
Article 39A (added by the 42nd Amendment) directs the State to provide equal justice and free legal aid.
It ensures that no citizen is denied justice due to economic or other disabilities.
Note: This led to the establishment of Lok Adalats and the Legal Services Authorities Act.

content.question: Which Article empowers Parliament to restrict fundamental rights for members of armed forces?
content.note:
Article 33 empowers Parliament to modify or restrict the Fundamental Rights of members of the Armed Forces, Paramilitary forces, police, and intelligence agencies.
This is necessary to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and maintenance of discipline.
Note: Only Parliament can make these laws, not state legislatures.

content.question: Which Article is related to the promotion of co-operative societies?
content.note:
Article 43B (added by the 97th Amendment) promotes the voluntary formation and democratic control of Cooperative Societies.
It is a Directive Principle of State Policy. Related info: It works in tandem with the Fundamental Right to form cooperatives under Article 19.

content.question: The position of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) was recommended by which Act?
content.note:
The Government of India Act, 1935 strengthened the institution of the Auditor-General (now CAG).
It made the office more independent to ensure financial accountability. Current Status: The Comptroller and Auditor General is a constitutional body under Article 148.

content.question: Who propounded the concept of the 'Rule of Law'?
content.note:
The concept of the Rule of Law was famously propounded by the British jurist A.V. Dicey.
It includes three elements: Absence of arbitrary power, Equality before the law, and Primacy of the rights of the individual.
Note: Indian Article 14 is a reflection of this concept.

content.question: Under whose leadership were Fundamental Duties added to the Constitution?
content.note:
Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution in 1976 under the leadership of Indira Gandhi.
This was done via the 42nd Amendment during the Internal Emergency.
Note: The aim was to remind citizens that while they have rights, they also have responsibilities toward the nation.

content.question: How many seats are reserved for women in municipalities or local bodies?
content.note:
The 73rd and 74th Amendments mandate that one-third (33.33%) of total seats in local bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) must be reserved for women.
This includes seats reserved for SC/ST women.
Note: Many Indian states have now increased this reservation to 50%.

content.question: Which Act provides measures to prevent offenders from evading the process of law while outside India?
content.note:
The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 targets individuals who have committed economic offenses and fled India to escape prosecution.
It allows the government to confiscate the properties of such offenders. Context: It was enacted to deal with high-profile bank fraud cases.

content.question: Who headed the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee in the Constituent Assembly in 1946?
content.note:
J.B. Kripalani was the chairman of the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee.
This sub-committee worked under the Advisory Committee headed by Sardar Patel.
Note: They formulated the draft of the rights that eventually became Part III of the Constitution.

content.question: The provision for the election of Rajya Sabha members was adopted from which country?
content.note:
The provision for the Election of members of the Rajya Sabha was adopted from the Constitution of South Africa.
In India, these members are elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies.
Note: This is different from the nomination of 12 members by the President.

content.question: Under which Article does a citizen have the freedom to practice any profession?
content.note:
Article 19(1)(g) guarantees all citizens the right to practice any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade, or business.
It is a Fundamental Right under the 'Right to Freedom'. Reasonable Restrictions: The state can impose restrictions in the interest of the general public or prescribe professional qualifications.

content.question: Which minorities are mentioned in Article 30?
content.note:
Article 30 mentions two types of minorities: Religious and Linguistic.
It grants these minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
Note: The term 'minority' is not explicitly defined in the Constitution itself.

content.question: Which Article defines separate secretarial staff for each House of Parliament?
content.note:
Article 98 provides that each House of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) shall have its own separate secretarial staff.
This ensures the independence of the Legislature from the Executive.
Note: Their recruitment and service conditions are regulated by Parliament.

content.question: In which judgment was it stated that 'Secularism' and 'Federalism' are basic features of the Constitution?
content.note:
In the S.R. Bommai case (1994), the Supreme Court held that Secularism and Federalism are parts of the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.
This means they cannot be removed or damaged by any constitutional amendment. Context: The case dealt with the dismissal of state governments under Article 356.
